patches.why: STRUCTURAL RECOVERY, read at the plate 2026-09-16 (prep spot check). Migne sets a display heading above this work and Corpus Corporum drops the whole line; our TEI body opened at CC's own catalogue title, which Migne does not print. Same class as the five Glossa Pentateuch book-title lines (Wilson's ruling 2026-09-06), encoded by the same convention: <head type="book-title"> above the first head, before the first column mark, so col is null. Witness: Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k5505319w, map f = (column + 1) / 2 (corners read FIRST: f6 = 11/12, f13 = 25/26, f15 = 29/30, f17 = 33/34, f18 = 35/36); this heading on f18 (cols 35/36). Transcribed with ae for the ligature as the TEI does; Migne's capitals, small capitals and italics are not encoded. Read at native resolution from a server-side crop. ⚑ Migne prints NO full stop after MCCCCXXIX before Quibus; transcribed as printed. The rubric is load-bearing: it names the addressee (Alphonsus, dean of Compostela, the author's son) and announces that Doring's Replicae are inserted. ⚑ Those Replicae (INCIPIT PROLOGUS IN Replicas defensivas, col 60B onward) are in no Corpus Corporum file.

patches.why: FOOT-OF-PAGE NOTE ANCHOR RESTORED, read at the plate 2026-09-16 (prep spot check). Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k5505319w f25, corners read FIRST = 49/50. Migne prints (a) after legis in col 50B, keyed to a note set under both columns: (a) Id est in eadem arbore nascentem in qua ramusculus. Corpus Corporum dropped both the key and the note. The key is encoded as the raised-letter glyph ª, the form inject-plate-notes.mjs reads for the letter layer (precedent 8949 @0256C), though Migne sets it in parentheses on the line. The note is recovered in data/plate-notes/8974.tsv and belongs to the asterisk/letter layer (editorial prose: [cn:] plus translated [nt:]).
